comment: Does the SKILL.md description attract the requests it should and repel the ones it shouldn't? Protocol: docs/darwin-benchmark.md item 5. dev queries probe; holdout queries judge a description change (re-test judged on holdout only).

queries.query: Design a poster for our campus music festival — A2 print, loud colors, huge headline.
queries.note: Sanity attractor: names the craft and the deliverable outright.

queries.query: Review this design — our landing page hero feels off and I can't tell why.
queries.note: The 'review this design' phrasing the description explicitly claims.

queries.query: Give me three options for a 404 screen that people actually smile at.
queries.note: Keyword-clean attractor: a UI deliverable described with none of the description's trigger words.

queries.query: Our quarterly numbers read like a wall of text — I need a one-glance handout the board can absorb in five minutes.
queries.note: Keyword-clean attractor: data made visual, without saying chart, dashboard, or infographic.

queries.query: The onboarding screens in my fitness app feel clunky — what would someone with taste change?
queries.note: Keyword-clean attractor: an improvement request for mobile UI phrased as taste, not design.

queries.query: Build a production web app for order management — Node, Postgres, JWT auth, and a REST API for the mobile client.
queries.note: The description's own negative boundary (not for production web apps or backend systems); it uses the boundary's words on purpose and must still repel.

queries.query: Refactor our ETL pipeline — split the ingest job, add retries, move the transforms into dbt models.
queries.note: Non-visual engineering; nothing here produces an artifact to judge.

queries.query: Code-review this PR: the retry logic in the payments service leaks connections.
queries.note: A 'review this' ask with nothing visual in it — the word review alone must not attract.

queries.query: Write the launch email — three subject lines, body copy, and CTA text.
queries.note: Copy is the deliverable itself; the skill supports copy tone only as part of visual work.

queries.query: Write a Go CLI that batch-renames photo files by their EXIF date.
queries.note: Purely functional tooling; photos are the input, not the deliverable.

queries.query: Translate our 12-page user manual from English to Japanese, keep the tone.
queries.note: A documents job other skills own; 'page' appears here and must not be enough to trigger.
